titulo: Explainer with avatar and voice: explicavideos under the hood
lead: explicavideos turns a script into an explainer video with avatar, voice, animated scenes and captions. Only one part is expensive: the avatar studio. In this lesson you run the engine's tests and build scenes, blocks and templates from a script of your own, stopping before the studio.
objetivo: run the explicavideos tests and build scenes and blocks from a script of your own without generating anything in the avatar studio.

aprende.t: The engine's stages, from script to finished video
The scene format: title, chapter, speech, labels and takeaway
Why scenes become blocks and what the per-block limit does
Where the studio gate is and what --help says the code does not do

hero_alt: A small dark studio with an empty stool, a microphone on a stand and an editing monitor with a split screen showing a slide and a presenter.

secoes.sub: Click each stage. Only the middle one spends credit.

nos.detalhe: A list of scenes with title, chapter, speech (the spoken line), labels (the on-screen labels), takeaway and source. The agent writes it; you review it.
The prepare step groups whole scenes into blocks up to the max_chars limit (4,400 in --help and in all the examples) and writes blocos/manifest.json. No spoken line is cut in the middle.

Each block becomes an avatar video in the HeyGen studio, using the subscription of whoever owns the avatar. It is the only step that spends credit, and it only runs with the start command. In commit 604fc74, what generates it is a Playwright script in the web studio, using the owner's profile and virtual screen from their environment: on another machine, start does not run without adaptation.
The avatar audio is transcribed with per-word timing (local Whisper or an external service, depending on the config). This is what syncs scene and speech.

In the v1 engine (explica.py), each block becomes a HyperFrames composition with the avatar in a corner, the scenes and the caption, and the blocks are assembled into one MP4. The v2 (engine/v2) redoes the visuals on top, reusing the avatar and transcript from v1.

secoes.volta: the manifest keeps track of where it stopped
secoes.legenda: Steps of the v1 engine, read from the README and the code of explicavideos 2.13.10 (commit 604fc74). The prepare step is the first step of both engines, v1 and v2. HyperFrames on the inside is the subject of course 3.

secoes.titulo: The engine at a pinned commit
secoes.sub: Clones it, shows the version, reads --help and runs the tests. The tests simulate the network and swap the render for a command that fails if called: nothing leaves your machine.

blocos.conteudo:
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-fabrica/a2; rm -rf "$E"; mkdir -p "$E"; cd "$E"
git clone -q https://github.com/inematds/explicavideos.git && cd explicavideos
git checkout -q 604fc74 && cat VERSION
python3 explica.py --help | grep -E "^  (prepare|preview)"
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests > testes.log 2>&1; echo "saída: $?"
grep -E "^(Ran|OK)" testes.log | sed 's/ in .*s$//'

abas.html:
2.13.10
  prepare   monta cenas, blocos (<= 4.400 caracteres) e templates. Não gera nada no HeyGen.
  preview   renderiza o bloco 1 localmente, sem avatar, para conferir o layout.
saída: 0
Ran 50 tests
OK

The block drops the time from the Ran 50 tests line (it changes on every run). Note the text of preview: it says it renders, but see the next tab.

At commit 604fc74, preview calls build_final_block.py pt 1 --preview, which only writes the HTML of block 1 to layout-preview/, with placeholder timings and the notice "PRÉVIA VISUAL · SEM NARRAÇÃO" in place of the avatar. No MP4 comes out. When the help text and the code disagree, the code wins.

secoes.titulo: A script of your own becomes scenes and blocks
secoes.sub: Four sample scenes and a config that points to them. The low limit (300 characters) is on purpose, to see the packing.

blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/formacao-cinema-ia-fabrica-v72/kit
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-fabrica/a2; cd "$E/explicavideos"
cat > "$E/ensaio.json" <<FIM
{"id": "ensaio", "title": "Ensaio", "source_repo": "$E", "output": "$E/saida",
 "languages": ["pt"], "scene_files": {"pt": "$K/exemplos/a2-explica/cenas-pt.json"},
 "max_chars": 300}
FIM
python3 explica.py --config "$E/ensaio.json" prepare; echo "saída: $?"
ls "$E/saida/blocos" "$E/saida/templates/pt"
python3 explica.py --config "$E/ensaio.json" status | head -3

abas.html:
{"blocks": 2, "scenes": 4, "topics": 0, "chars": 561}
saída: 0
/tmp/ensaio-fabrica/a2/saida/blocos:
manifest.json
pt-b01.txt
pt-b02.txt

/tmp/ensaio-fabrica/a2/saida/templates/pt:
scene-01.html
scene-02.html
scene-03.html
scene-04.html
{
  "submitted": {
    "prepared": 2

Two scenes per block (155 + 123 characters fit in 300; the third does not). The status command shows both blocks as prepared: nothing was sent to the studio. The scene-NN.html templates already have a data-duration calculated from the speech.

secoes.sub: The engine refuses to cut a speech. With the limit at 140, the first scene (155 characters) already overflows.

blocos.conteudo:
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-fabrica/a2; cd "$E/explicavideos"
sed 's/"max_chars": 300/"max_chars": 140/' "$E/ensaio.json" > "$E/curto.json"
sed -i 's#"output": "[^"]*"#"output": "'"$E"'/saida-curta"#' "$E/curto.json"
python3 explica.py --config "$E/curto.json" prepare 2>&1 | grep -E "^ValueError"; echo "saída: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

abas.html:
ValueError: Scene 1 exceeds limit; split its narration before submitting
saída: 1

The fix is to split the scene's speech in two, not to raise the limit: the real limit comes from the studio.

secoes.titulo: The start: five services that resume where they stopped
secoes.sub: In real production, start brings up five services. Run it, interrupt it and run it again.

msg.inicio: 5 steps in fila/. Click "Run the queue".
msg.rodando: Each service reads and writes the manifest: that is how it knows what has already been done.
msg.parou: Interrupted. The middle step stayed in rodando/. Run it again to see the resume.
msg.retoma: Resume: what the manifest already lists as sent is not sent again. Sending again = generating again = spending credit.
msg.fim: Empty queue: video assembled and published.
msg.fimfalha: Empty queue. The render went to falhou/: you redo only the render, without touching the studio.

secoes.legenda: Browser simulation: nothing really runs. The five names are the start services in explicavideos 2.13.10 (submit, monitor, render, assemble, publish).

secoes.sub: Three things to check before any start.

texto: The engine's --help requires an APROVADO_HEYGEN file in the output, with the avatar owner's authorization and the number of blocks and minutes. It is a written rule, not a block in the code: your gate (lesson 7) is what really closes it.
The engine was built for Nei's avatar and voice, with his consent. In your use, the avatar is yours, with a signed consent form. Someone else's avatar without a consent form, no.

Profiles belong to v2: without profile_visual, you get the aula profile; with "profile_visual": "viral", the viral profile (faster cuts), checked by engine/v2/qa_viral.py, which prints APROVADO, APROVADO COM AVISO or REPROVADO.

The v2 does not generate the avatar again: it starts from a finished v1 production and redoes the visuals of each block with a visual script driven by spoken cues, the same concept the refazvideo validator checks in lesson 4.
README commands (only described here, because they need the avatar's transcribed speech): engine/v2/setup_output.py → engine/v2/build_block.py 1 --strict → engine/v2/run_lane.sh 1 2 3.

secoes.titulo: What comes out of the engine
secoes.sub: A 10-minute explainer made with explicavideos v2, with Nei's own avatar and voice (with his consent), in three languages.
From the tested engine to the scenes of your next video.

exercicios.texto: Run the "prepare and status" block with the kit's four scenes.

Ask your agent for the scenes of an explainer of your own (5 to 8 scenes, each spoken line up to 600 characters) in the same format as cenas-pt.json. Save it to ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-fabrica/a2/minhas-cenas.json, change the scene_files in the config, and run prepare with max_chars 4400.
exercicios.pronto: cd ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-fabrica/a2/explicavideos && python3 explica.py --config ../ensaio.json prepare; echo "saída: $?" → one line {"blocks": …, "scenes": N, …} with the N of your scenes and saída: 0.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after you answer.

perguntas.explica: start brings up the services, and the first one (submit) generates video in the avatar studio. prepare, status and preview are local.

perguntas.p: A scene has 5,000 characters of speech and the limit is 4,400. What do you do?
opcoes: Split the speech into two scenes.
perguntas.explica: The limit comes from the studio, per block. The engine refuses to cut a line of speech in the middle (ValueError: Scene … exceeds limit); the way out is to split the scene.

perguntas.p: The --help says preview renders; the code only writes an HTML file. Which one do you trust?
opcoes: The --help, because it's the official documentation.
The code, and note the mismatch.
perguntas.explica: When the docs and the code disagree, the code wins. Run it and see what comes out in layout-preview/ before promising an MP4.

perguntas.p: Why does the manifest matter when start is interrupted?
opcoes: Because it deletes the blocks already downloaded to free up disk space.
Because it stores the avatar studio password.
Because it speeds up the render of the following blocks.
Because it says what has already been sent to the studio.
perguntas.explica: Each service reads the manifest and only does what's left. A block that was already sent doesn't go back to the studio: sending it again means generating it again.

itens.texto: speech is for hearing, labels are for seeing; the agent writes, you review.
prepare packs whole scenes up to the studio limit, without spending anything.
the only paid step sits behind start, approval and your consent form.
